nodes.name: Two-step annealing for PtMn catalyst
nodes.procedure: Catalyst with the coexistence of bimetallic PtMn_AC and Pt_SA anchored on sulfur-doped carbon by two-step low temperature annealing. ICPMS analysis indicates that the Pt loading in PtMn_AC/Pt_SA SC is approximately 3.6 wt%, half of other catalysts, which occurs because, during the initial heating process, the Pt and Mn precursors competitively interact for a limited number of sulfur anchoring sites on the carbon support.
nodes.source_text: As illustrated in Figure 1a, we synthesized catalyst with the coexistence of bimetallic PtMn_AC and Pt_SA anchored on sulfur-doped carbon by two-step low temperature annealing.

nodes.description: HER LSV polarization curves in three-electrode setup
nodes.source_text: HER performance was first evaluated with a three-electrode setup in Ar-saturated 0.5 M H2SO4 solution. Linear sweep voltammograms (LSV) polarization curves reveal that PtMn_{AC} / Pt_{SA}SC displays the lowest overpotential of 13 mV at a current density of 100 mA cm^{-2} ... highest mass activity of 14.48 A mg^{-1}Pt at an overpotential of 15 mV ... Tafel slopes ... 14.1 mV dec^{-1}

The HER catalytic activity and stability of PtMn_AC / Pt_SA SC were then assessed under practical working conditions in a PEMWE (1×1 cm) using commercial IrO2 as the anode ... PtMn_AC / Pt_SA SC can deliver high current density of 1, 2, and 3 A cm^{-2} with cell voltage of 1.82, 2.10, and 2.43 V, respectively ... operating for 160 h at 0.5 A cm^{-2} with a low potential degradation rate of only 0.14 mV h^{-1}

nodes.description: HER LSV polarization curves in three-electrode setup
nodes.source_text: outperforms the commercial 40 wt% Pt/C (39 mV) ... 41-fold ... commercial 40 wt% Pt/C (35.4 mV dec^{-1})

PtMn_AC / Pt_SA SC can deliver high current density of 1, 2, and 3 A cm^{-2} with cell voltage of 1.82, 2.10, and 2.43 V, respectively, superior to 40 wt% Pt/C ... low potential degradation rate of only 0.14 mV h^{-1}, which is significantly lower than that of 40 wt% Pt/C (1.44 mV h^{-1})

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS demonstrates sulfur atoms in thiophene-like S (C-S-C) form with small amount of oxidized S species (C-SO_x) on the sulfur-doped carbon support.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) in Figure S1 demonstrates that sulfur atoms are in form of thiophene-like S (C-S-C), along with a small amount of oxidized S species (C - SO_x).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD analyses show two broad diffraction peaks at 24° and 44° corresponding to the (002) and (101) diffraction planes of graphitized disordered amorphous carbon. No diffraction peaks corresponding to crystalline Pt were detected.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) analyses show two broad diffraction peaks at 24° and 44° corresponding to the (002) and (101) diffraction planes of graphitized disordered amorphous carbon ... No diffraction peaks corresponding to crystalline Pt were detected in the XRD pattern of PtMn_AC / Pt_SA SC.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images reveal that PtMn_AC / Pt_SA SC inherits the 2D ultrathin sheet of ketjen black with rough surface and does not show visible metal nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images reveal that PtMn_AC / Pt_SA SC inherits the 2D ultrathin sheet of ketjen black with rough surface and does not show visible metal nanoparticles (Figure S7).

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM images show numerous bright atomic clusters with <1 nm size. Aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM shows coexistence of single atoms and bimetallic atomic clusters by bright dots. Several Pt atoms scatter around the clusters (~8Å) with a distance around 4Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-angle annular dark-field scanning TEM (HAADF-STEM) images show numerous bright atomic clusters with < 1 nm size ... Aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM shows noticeable coexistence of single atoms and bimetallic atomic clusters by bright dots.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mappings confirm the homogeneous distribution of Pt, Mn, S and C elements.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the corresponding energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) mappings confirm the homogeneous distribution of Pt, Mn, S and C elements (Figure 1c,d and S8).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICPMS analysis indicates Pt loading of 3.6 wt% in PtMn_AC / Pt_SA SC, 6.8 wt% in Pt_SA / SC, 7.3 wt% in Pt_AC / SC, and 7.5 wt% in Pt_AC / Pt_SA SC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry (ICPMS) analysis indicates that the Pt loading in PtMn_AC / Pt_SA SC is approximately 3.6 wt%, half of Pt_SA / SC (6.8 wt%), Pt_AC / SC (7.3 wt%), and Pt_AC / Pt_SA SC (7.5 wt%) (Table S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt 4f XPS spectra show Pt^δ+ (atomically dispersed) and Pt^0 (clustered) species in Pt_AC/Pt_SA SC and PtMn_AC/Pt_SA SC; only Pt^δ+ in Pt_SA/SC. Mn 2p XPS shows oxidized Mn species in PtMn_AC/Pt_SA SC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the Pt 4f XPS spectra (Figure 2a), both Pt_AC / Pt_SA SC and PtMn_AC / Pt_SA SC exhibit two Pt 4f doublets corresponding to electron-deficient Pt^δ+ (atomically dispersed Pt) and metallic Pt^0 (clustered Pt), whereas Pt_SA / SC shows only the Pt^δ+ species. Figure 2b indicates the presence of Mn species of PtMn_AC / Pt_SA SC with oxidized state.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt L-edge XANES shows lower white-line energy for PtMn_AC / Pt_SA SC indicating increased Pt 5d occupancy. Mn K-edge XANES shows average Mn oxidation state between Mn^2+ and Mn^4+.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Pt L-edge XANES spectra (Figure 2c), which show a lower white-line energy for PtMn_AC / Pt_SA SC than for Pt_AC / Pt_SA SC and Pt_SA / SC, indicating increased Pt 5d occupancy.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt L-edge EXAFS shows Pt-S at ~1.77Å (C.N. 3.4), Pt-Mn at 2.54Å (C.N. 0.7), Pt-Pt at 2.74Å (C.N. 4.1). Mn K-edge shows Mn-Pt at ~2.70Å. ~80% Pt in PtMn clusters, 20% as single atoms.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) at the Pt L-edge (Figure 2e) displays a dominant peak at ~1.77Å attributable to Pt-S coordination ... Quantitative EXAFS fitting in R-space (Table S3) yields an average Pt-S coordination number (C.N.) of 3.4.

nodes.characterization_summary: H2-TPD shows two desorption features at ~100°C and ~600°C corresponding to H2 release from Pt_SA and PtMn_AC sites. Main peak of PtMn_AC / Pt_SA SC centers at lower temperature 90°C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Hydrogen temperature-programmed desorption (H2-TPD) measurements reveal two desorption features at ~100 and ~600°C, corresponding to H2 release from Pt_SA and PtMn_AC sites, respectively (Figure 5f).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ FTIR spectra of CO adsorption reveal the coexistence of multiscale sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In situ FTIR spectra of CO adsorption reveal the coexistence of multiscale sites and theoretical calculations elucidate the formation mechanism of stable PtMn_AC, which confirm the rationality of the existence of PtMn_AC (Figures S9, S10).
